exposure: Women who underwent cesarean section without myomectomy
cervical and cornual localization of myomas
outcome: Short-term surgical outcomes (e.g., blood loss, operative time)
Long-term outcomes (e.g., myoma recurrence, pregnancy outcomes)
cohort: Women who underwent cesarean section with or without myomectomy
finding: Cesarean myomectomy was associated with a relatively low rate of myoma recurrence, and subsequent pregnancy appeared to be protective against recurrence without increasing the risk of complications like adhesion formation.
mod_finding: Cesarean myomectomy was associated with a low rate of myoma recurrence and subsequent pregnancy did not increase adhesion formation or obstetric complications.
